title: Science starts with imagination.
label: CREATIVE
intro: Explore the art of asking what if—and the craft of finding out.
sections: Ask what if
Use familiar scientific ideas as starting points for thought experiments. Question assumptions and imagine how a change might affect the world around you.
See ideas differently
Look for patterns in nature and use comparisons to explain difficult concepts. A useful analogy can make an unfamiliar idea easier to approach.
Create and reflect
Try a small, safe project, record what happened, and consider what you would change. Creative science includes testing, mistakes and revision.

title: Build skills for a curious life.
label: SKILLS
intro: Clear thinking, communication and careful observation grow through practice.
sections: Think critically
Examine evidence, distinguish claims from conclusions, and break a difficult problem into manageable steps.
Explain clearly
Use everyday language and useful examples to communicate an idea. Connect knowledge from different subjects while keeping the explanation accurate.
Observe carefully
Make predictions, notice details, and record results. Practical activities help turn curiosity into a method for learning.

title: Follow a question somewhere new.
label: EXPLORE
intro: Discover connections between science, creativity and everyday experience.
sections: Understand the foundations
Explore physics, chemistry and biology through the forces, materials and living systems that shape our world.
Find science in daily life
Look at cooking, movement and familiar technology through scientific questions. Everyday experiences can open the door to bigger ideas.
Connect and imagine
Use thought experiments and creative explanations to investigate possibilities. Compare claims with evidence and keep asking how and why.

title: Make understanding the goal.
label: LEARNING
intro: Stories and examples can turn an intimidating topic into an inviting question.
sections: Begin with curiosity
Find a question that interests you. Stories and real-world situations give abstract ideas a useful context.
Build the explanation
Connect a new idea with something familiar. Work through the reasoning step by step, then check the limits of the comparison.
Try it yourself
Explain what you learned in your own words, make a prediction, or test your understanding with a question. Return to the parts that remain unclear.
